svg.title: Threat modeling a Bedrock application: one threat and one control per element
svg.desc: A chat front end sends user prompts through Bedrock Guardrails to a model that retrieves from a knowledge base built on an S3 bucket and calls tools through an agent, with logs and an API endpoint. Prompt: injection, countered by the guardrails prompt attack filter. Knowledge base documents: poisoning, countered by limiting who can write to the S3 bucket. Model response: disclosure, countered by sensitive information filters. Tools: excessive agency, countered by least-privilege roles and separate approval. Logs: repudiation, countered by invocation logging and CloudTrail. API endpoint: denial of service and runaway cost, countered by quotas and token budgets.
svg.text: Threat modeling a Bedrock application: one threat and one control per element

g.text: restrict writes to the S3 bucket; review
When you add a tool, a data source, or a model, update the threat model in the same change and turn each row into a test.
